public_rationale: Alphabet's cash flow data show FY2024 purchases of property and equipment of $52.5 billion. That is a little above the $50 billion he cited. Capex for 2019-2023 was $23.5B, $22.3B, $24.6B, $31.5B and $32.3B, an average of about $26.8B. So FY2024 was about 1.96 times that average, and his $50B figure would be 1.86 times. Either way, 'nearly double' holds. Alphabet's CFO said the spending went mainly to servers and data centers, which matches his 'data centers and GPUs'. The 'killed its golden goose' line is a metaphor and is not scored.
limitations: Capex figures come from aggregators reproducing Alphabet's 10-K, not from the SEC page itself.
The rhetorical claim that search has been 'killed' is not assessed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Google has essentially killed its golden goose, search, and is now spending its proceeds on data centers and GPUs, raising its capital expenditures in financial year 2024 to $50 billion, nearly double its average capital expenditures from 2019 to 2023.

statement.excerpt: If you’ll forgive the mixed metaphors, Google has essentially killed its golden goose — search — and is now in the process of pawning its eggs to buy decidedly non-magical beans, by which I mean data centers and GPUs, with Google increasing its capital expenditures in the financial year 2024 to $50 billion, equivalent to nearly double its average capital expenditures from 2019 to 2023.

from_speaker: increasing its capital expenditures in the financial year 2024 to $50 billion
nearly double its average capital expenditures from 2019 to 2023
our_interpretation: The checkable core is Alphabet's FY2024 capital expenditures (purchases of property and equipment) compared with its 2019-2023 annual average, and whether that spending went mainly to data centers and servers/GPUs.
'Killed its golden goose' is a rhetorical metaphor and is not scored.
At the post date FY2024 was not over; the reported full-year figure is used to test it. '$50 billion' is read as roughly $50 billion; 'nearly double' is read as a ratio of about 1.8x to 2.0x.
criteria.support_condition: Alphabet's reported FY2024 capex is about $50 billion or more, is roughly 1.8x-2.0x the 2019-2023 average, and goes mainly to technical infrastructure such as servers and data centers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reported FY2024 capex well below $50 billion, or a ratio to the 2019-2023 average well short of double (for example under 1.6x).
